# Frontend Design Rules

## RTL (Right-to-Left) Awareness

**CRITICAL**: RTL is one of the most common sources of UI bugs.

- **Flex order is reversed**: In RTL, first child appears on RIGHT, last child on LEFT
- **RTL must propagate**: Inner flex containers may not inherit `dir="rtl"`
- **Text alignment**: Hebrew/Arabic text should be `text-right`, `items-end`
- **Use screen positions**: Say "LEFT side of screen" not "first in DOM"

When working on ANY Hebrew/Arabic UI, explicitly verify RTL layout.

## Component Guidelines

- Keep components small and focused (single responsibility)
- Use semantic HTML elements (`<button>`, `<nav>`, `<article>`, etc.)
- Prefer Tailwind utility classes over custom CSS
- Always include proper ARIA labels for accessibility
- Test on mobile viewport sizes

## React Patterns

- Use hooks, not class components
- Memoize expensive calculations with `useMemo`
- Use `useCallback` for functions passed to child components
- Avoid inline arrow functions in JSX when passing to children
- Keep state as close as possible to where it's used

## Accessibility

- All interactive elements must be keyboard accessible
- Images need alt text
- Forms need proper labels
- Color contrast must meet WCAG AA standards
- Test with screen readers when possible
